subject: Model-generated content title & consent — MSA and Order Form alignment
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@furnishco.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model-generated content title & consent — MSA and Order Form alignment

Hi Maya — great to be moving forward. Quick item from procurement/legal that popped up during our draft review: FurnishCo would like clarity on who holds title to content produced by the model when your users generate product descriptions and imagery via the integration.

Specifically they asked whether Redwood (as the service provider) can assert any ownership over model-generated content, and whether we would be allowed to use FurnishCo-generated content to further train or improve models (feedback/training rights).

High level: FurnishCo's ask is to retain exclusive title to output created via their account and to prevent Redwood from using that content to train models. Our typical position is to grant customers ownership or broad rights to use outputs while negotiating a limited, non-identifying feedback license for quality improvements.

Can Laura / Soojin weigh in on a defensible position we can propose that keeps the deal moving? I attached the current redline and a short proposed snippet we could offer. If you prefer, we can propose a two-tier approach: (1) customer owns and controls distribution of model outputs; (2) Redwood may retain a narrow, aggregated feedback license that is explicitly excluded from training models for commercial purposes unless customer opts in.

Next steps: let me know a clean line to put back into the MSA/Order Form today and I'll send as a tracked-change suggestion.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@furnishco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Model-generated content title & consent — MSA and Order Form alignment

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick update. FurnishCo's legal and product teams are aligned on two core points:

1) We need explicit assignment or an exclusive, perpetual right to title in all content generated by FurnishCo users via the service (product copy, imagery, configuration outputs). We will not accept ambiguous "customer grants" language that leaves ownership open.

2) Separately, FurnishCo will not permit Redwood to use any such content to train or refine models, even in aggregate, without prior written permission for a specific program. We are open to a telemetry-style, non-content feedback option (error rates, anonymized usage metrics) but not training on our content.

If Redwood can put a concrete proposed clause in the MSA/Order Form that mirrors the above, we can circulate internally and aim to close next week. Attaching a short note from our counsel summarizing our position.

Best,
Maya

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Model-generated content title & consent — MSA and Order Form alignment

Thanks for the ping, Ben. Quick summary and proposed path that keeps the commercial terms moving while protecting Redwood's model development practices: 

Key points we can offer back to FurnishCo (redlines attached):

1) Title to Outputs: we can agree that FurnishCo (or FurnishCo's end users) will have ownership or an exclusive, perpetual license to use, reproduce, and distribute model-generated content produced by their account — i.e., they get effective control over the outputs for productization and commercialization. We should avoid wording that says Redwood "assigns" title in a way that carries implied warranties beyond our standard representations. Instead use "Customer shall retain exclusive rights, title, and interest in and to Output" with carveouts for our underlying service (the model/service code).

2) Training / Feedback: propose a split approach — (a) Redwood will not use Customer Output to train or fine-tune any models or for model parameter updates without prior written consent; (b) Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, de-identified telemetry and system metrics (e.g., prompt latency, error rates, anonymized token frequency summaries) for service improvement and safety monitoring. Include explicit language prohibiting re-identification and dictating retention windows.

3) Optional Opt-in: add a narrowly scoped opt-in that allows Customer to permit Redwood to use Customer Output for a specific training program (defined by scope, timeframe, and intended use) under a separate, signed agreement and with an explicit compensation arrangement. This preserves commercial fairness and keeps training programs visible and auditable.

4) Indemnity and Risk: make sure we exclude implied warranties about outputs and include mutual representations that Customer controls the input data and has rights to have it processed. Avoid broad indemnities tied to model improvements — those belong in product-specific schedules if at all.

Action for Ben: send FurnishCo the attached tracked-changes redline and the short clause text below. If they accept, Legal will prepare a final MSA/Order Form insert and the opt-in exhibit for training programs.

Proposed clause (short form to include in Order Form):
"Customer Output. Customer shall retain exclusive rights, title and interest in and to all Content, data and other materials generated by or on behalf of Customer using the Service (\"Customer Output\"). Redwood may not use Customer Output to train, fine-tune or otherwise update the parameters of any model or algorithm without Customer's prior written consent executed as a separate agreement. Redwood may, however, collect and use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and metrics for the purpose of service monitoring, safety, and non-training product improvements, subject to reasonable technical and contractual safeguards against re-identification and limited retention periods."

I've attached a tracked redline edition of the MSA and a brief Order Form snippet you can send to FurnishCo. For transparency, include the opt-in exhibit language so procurement sees the alternative.

Let me know if you want me on the call with Maya and procurement; happy to join to close language quickly.
